text.p: Portuguese bonds finished slightly lower along with Spanish Bonos but dealers said the absence of investors in the local market prevented steeper losses.

"Negative spreads with Spain have widened which makes me think that if Spain continues to head down tomorrow, there will be more liquidity here and stronger selling. Spreads should not widen to more than -20 basis points," said one trader.
If Bonos are steady then the Portuguese market is likely to remain stagnant, he said.
The escudo ended at 102.56/59 per mark, barely changed from its opening 102.55/58.
